pr_title: Allow restoration of empty files by recovery tool

issue_context.title: 0-byte files are not restored with RecoveryTool
issue_context.body:
The tool `Duplicati.CommandLine.RecoveryTool.exe` is faulty.
It does not restore empty (0 byte) files properly.
I tried it on:
- Linux*
- Wine on Linux (Ubuntu)
- Windows 11

All these systems did not restore the 0-size files.
These files are critical in database operation.
<details>
  <summary>*Linux is buggy</summary>

Backslash path separator is wrong: `\`. It should be `/`

Restoring Windows backup of file `file.jpg` in directory `myDirectory` is buggy on Linux because:

Windows path is `myDirectory\file.jpg`

RecoveryTool then restores it as:
```shell
$ ls -la
'myDirectory\file.jpg'
```
❌ Which does not create `myDirectory`, but *a file named with a windows slash path* 🤦 
✅ It should create a directory: `myDirectory` and then `file.jpg` - with linux path `myDirectory/file.jpg`
</details>

- [x] I have searched open and closed issues for duplicates.
- [x] I have searched the [forum](https://forum.duplicati.com) for related topics.
https://forum.duplicati.com/t/recoverytool-error/8673/5
----------------------------------------

## Environment info
<!-- Please include some relevant information about your environment. -->
<!-- For "Backend", please indicate the backup destination (e.g. Amazon S3, OneDrive, FTP, WebDAV, local). -->
- **Duplicati version**: duplicati-2.0.6.3_beta_2021-06-17.
- **Operating system**: Windows 11
- **Backend**: Samba/SMB on Linux (Debian)


## Description
<!-- Describe the issue that you are experiencing below. -->
Zero-byte files are not restored with the `Duplicati.CommandLine.RecoveryTool.exe` program.

## Steps to reproduce
<!-- List the steps to reproduce the bug if possible. -->
1. Create files with 0 size. Maybe using Carestream database.
2. Backup using Duplicati on Windows
3. Run `Duplicati.CommandLine.RecoveryTool.exe restore`


<!-- For "Actual result", describe what happens after you run the steps above (i.e. buggy behavior). -->
<!-- For "Expected result", describe what should happen after you run the steps above (i.e. corrected behavior). -->
- **Actual result**:
⛔ Exception is thrown and file not created
- **Expected result**:
✅ File being created

comments:
Even though I agree this is an issue, backupping databases from the filesystem is generally a bad idea™. Decent databases provide data backup facilities, either through an SQL dump or through a specific tool.

(I'm not part of the duplicati team) 
Edit: Thanks for making the .zip format so simple! It was easy to read all backups in Rust instead of C# :smile: 

:crab: https://github.com/7ERr0r/duplicati-restore-rs
So `RecoveryTool`-like program in Rust uses 2x less RAM. And works out of the box without the `index` subcommand.

`RecoveryTool`:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6555818/212412943-794480b4-c8c7-4af7-aebc-1192cddfab90.png)


`rust-duplicati-restore`:
![Taskmgr_ukWCBFEoCH](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6555818/212425175-4e68ba9c-2509-45aa-975c-1246efe385a1.png)

In both cases `source` and `target` are on an SMB server. 
Therefore, it's weird the C# version uses my regular drive... why??
As a wild guess, I wonder if this fell through the cracks when empty files were made a special case instead of usual case but with actual empty block stored in the destination dblock file. This apparently caused trouble, so was changed, which caused trouble...

[Fixed empty block handling.](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/commit/4d98960e7546bb6306f834ca0a31a6755e885858#diff-ac0c80a394604994a796ba399278a43b)
[Fixed empty block handling in concurrent_processing branch #2637](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/pull/2637/files)
(note RestoreHandler.cs change, however I think RecoveryTool's restore process is quite a bit different -- somebody could verify)
Thanks to @gpatel-fr for being quick on a PR for the current issue (and thanks for noticing). Release production is slow currently because release manager has had no time, but it's nice to have some things in the queue for when needed volunteers are found.

[Empty source file can make Recreate download all dblock files fruitlessly with huge delay #3747](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/issues/3747) was previous regression noticed.
[Check block size on recreate #3758](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/pull/3758/files) was the one-line cure after a difficult chase...

> Therefore, it's weird the C# version uses my regular drive... why??

Regular restore and backup (and more) use lots of temporary files. Temporary folder is configured by `tempdir` option and more.
RecoveryTool has at least one temporary file usage that I noticed, [here](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/CommandLine/RecoveryTool/Restore.cs#L168). Possibly that's the use? File name likely starts with `dup-`.
If that doesn't reveal, Process Monitor on Windows or strace on Linux could probably reveal. I don't read C# all that well though.

> program in Rust

Thanks for that addition to the tool chest. There's also a Python script, and now I wonder whether that tool restores empty files...
[Independent restore program](https://forum.duplicati.com/t/independent-restore-program/2316)
[restore_from_python.py](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/master/Tools/Commandline/RestoreFromPython/restore_from_python.py)

review_comments: How can size be anything other than 0 if there are no hashes?

I'm not sure how quickly review comments can be processed. As explained elsewhere, there's a still-broken Canary to fix. 

Fortunately I know a bit about this one. See #4884 cited above for some history, and see [Processing a large file](https://duplicati.readthedocs.io/en/latest/appendix-a-how-the-backup-process-works/#processing-a-large-file) for how blocklists are only used for files with more than 1 block. [Processing a small file](https://duplicati.readthedocs.io/en/latest/appendix-a-how-the-backup-process-works/#processing-a-small-file) only has a size and a hash, but the history cited in the issue explains how a zero length block isn't in the backup files, though its hash might make one think that...

You can see the large file blocklist expansion in the else below the code in question, which handles the small file case, and presumably relies on its file open (without data written from a block) to make the empty file. That's my impression of this.

[Database rebuild](https://forum.duplicati.com/t/database-rebuild/13884/7?u=ts678) was my attempt as part of a team effort to summarize how things fit together. There are lots of hashes, and a blocklist is a block, and is known by its hash, and the filelist.json in the dlist file will have one or more for a large file.
